$comment: DriveOne Direct abandoned PAYMENT series. Audience: signed the contract, Ascent issued a contract number, started the Budco 0% plan, never completed funding (Supabase quotes.status=payment_pending, payment_status=budco_initiated, no budco_ric_url). This is NOT the abandoned quote drip (dod-abandon-e01..e08). Voice: Red Bull register. Deadpan, absurd, confident. No exclamation points. No em dashes or en dashes. Never call it a warranty. Never say the customer is covered: the contract is written, not active, until Budco funds it. Lead with the monthly and the down payment; never restate the full contract total. 0% in every email. One hero per email. No invented deadlines. Optional `video` block on an email renders a thumbnail card after the P.S. callout: one video max per email, never above the primary button, caption written in our voice (never the YouTube title). Test arm per SEQUENCE.md.

campaign.name: DriveOne Direct: Finish Your Payment
campaign.audience: driveonedirect.com customers who signed and started a Budco payment plan but did not complete it
campaign.exitOn: quotes.status = paid (Budco confirmed). Daily suppression job unsubscribes with suppressed_reason=purchased.
campaign.variablesNote: FIRST_NAME and RESEND_UNSUBSCRIBE_URL are Resend built-ins; never declare them. Fallbacks must never look numeric. RESUME_URL is the pre-filled quote link (year, make, mileage, term, ref, UTMs, #quote). Decided by Ryan 2026-10-12. It reopens checkout with the vehicle and term filled in; it does not resume the signed Budco session.

emails.goal: Name exactly where they stopped. Make finishing feel like the smallest thing on their list.
emails.subject: Your {{{VEHICLE}}} contract is one click short
emails.subjectAlt: {{{FIRST_NAME}}}, you stopped at the easy part
emails.preheader: The contract is written. It is waiting on the payment you already built.
emails.headline:
You did the hard part.
Then you stopped at the
easy part.
body: You picked a plan for your {{{VEHICLE}}}. You signed. The contract exists, with a number and everything. Then the payment screen happened and something else won.
Statistically it was a phone call, a child, or a cat on the keyboard. We do not judge. We just noticed.

hero.label: TO FINISH IT
hero.fine: 0% APR. No finance charge. No credit check. That is the plan, not a teaser.

emails.after: Nothing reset. Nothing expired. The link below reopens checkout for your {{{VEHICLE}}} with the same plan and term, ready to pay.
emails.ctaNote: Takes about as long as reading this sentence twice.
emails.ps: Over the next few weeks you will get one short email at a time about what this coverage actually does for your {{{VEHICLE}}}. No countdown clocks. An unsubscribe link on every one.

emails.goal: Remove the practical blocker. Budco payment help line and the two reasons payments fail.
emails.subject: If the payment page fought back
emails.subjectAlt: A form should not be the hardest part of owning a {{{VEHICLE}}}
emails.preheader: Two things stop most payments. Both are fixable in under five minutes.
emails.headline:
A payment form should
never be the hardest part
of owning a car.
body: If you stopped because the page gave you trouble, that is on us to fix, not you. Nearly every stalled payment comes down to one of two things.

One: the card declined or the bank wanted a second look. Two: the page timed out between signing and paying. Both are boring. Both are five minute fixes. The link below reopens checkout with your {{{VEHICLE}}} filled in; Budco can also finish it over the phone against your contract number.

hero.label: STILL THE SAME NUMBERS
hero.fine: 0% APR. Budco runs the payment plan. Ascent runs the coverage. We run the website. Everyone stays in their lane.

emails.after: Budco is the payment company behind the 0% plan. They are good on the phone and they will not try to sell you anything, because they do not have anything to sell you.
emails.ctaNote: Or call Budco at 888-352-7901, weekdays. Say the contract number.
emails.ps: If it was neither of those and you just changed your mind, that is allowed. Hit unsubscribe and we will go quietly.

video.title: The payment step, in real time
video.line: 31 seconds on a phone. No cuts. This is the checkout the link below opens.
video.note: Card is hidden until url is set. See VIDEO-E2-PAYMENT.md.

emails.goal: Make 0% believable. Address the catch everyone is waiting for.
emails.subject: Zero is not a promotion. It is a number.
emails.subjectAlt: The rate on your {{{VEHICLE}}} plan, in one digit
emails.preheader: No intro period. No step up at month seven. The rate is the rate.
emails.headline:
You are waiting for
the catch. We checked.
There is not one.
body: Most 0% offers are a magic trick. Zero for six months, then a rate that would embarrass a pawn shop. Yours is not that.
Your plan is 0% APR for the whole term. There is no finance charge, no deferred interest, no balloon payment waiting at the end like a surprise party nobody wanted.

hero.label: THE ENTIRE MATH
hero.fine: Add those up and you get your contract price. Not a dollar more. That is what 0% means when it is real.

emails.after: No credit check either. Budco does not pull your credit for this plan, so a 0% plan does not cost you a point on your score to find out about.
emails.ps: If you want to pay it all at once instead, you can do that on the same page. Some people like the feeling. We respect it.

emails.goal: The $100 deductible. Repairs are the only part of ownership with no sticker price.
emails.subject: The only part of your {{{VEHICLE}}} with no price tag
emails.subjectAlt: A repair bill is a surprise party you have to pay for
emails.preheader: Everything about your car has a known price except the thing that breaks.
emails.headline:
Every part of car ownership
has a price tag.
Except the repair.
body: You know the payment. You know the insurance. You know roughly what gas costs, because you have been angry about it.
The one number you do not know is the repair. It shows up at a time of its own choosing, with a figure of its own choosing, and it does not take questions.

hero.label: THE KNOWN NUMBER
hero.fine: Still {{{MONTHLY}}} a month at 0% APR. The plan replaces the one unknown number with two known ones.

emails.after: A transmission has never once negotiated. A $100 deductible has never once changed its mind. Pick which one you want to deal with.
emails.cta: Make the repair a known number →
emails.ctaNote: Reopens your {{{VEHICLE}}} checkout. Contract {{{CONTRACT}}} stays on file.
emails.ps: Reminder: coverage is not active until the payment goes through. The contract is written. It is not working yet.

emails.goal: Any ASE-certified shop. No captive dealer. We pay the shop directly.
emails.subject: You pick the shop. We pay the shop.
emails.subjectAlt: No, you do not have to drive it back to where you bought it
emails.preheader: Any ASE-certified repair shop in the country. Your mechanic counts.
emails.headline:
Your mechanic.
Your choice.
Our bill.
body: Some plans make you drive back to the dealership that sold you the car, which is a strange thing to require when the dealership is in another state and the car is on a flatbed.
Yours does not. Any ASE-certified shop in the country. The guy you trust. The place near work. The one your brother in law swears by, if you are feeling brave.

card.title: HOW A CLAIM GOES
rows: Take the {{{VEHICLE}}} to any ASE-certified shop
Shop calls Ascent at 866-660-7003 before work starts
We pay the shop. You pay $100.
You drive home. Nobody calls you later.

hero.label: WHAT THIS COSTS YOU
hero.fine: Openbay+ is included too, so if you do not have a shop you trust yet, you can book an ASE-certified one from your phone.

emails.after: The shop calls the administrator before touching anything. That one phone call is the whole claims process. There is no form, no receipt to mail, no reimbursement to wait for.
emails.ctaNote: Your vehicle and term are already filled in.
emails.ps: ASE-certified means the technician passed a national exam. It does not mean they will be nice to you. That part is on the shop.

emails.goal: Diminished Value Protection, up to $5,000. The benefit nobody else includes.
emails.subject: Your {{{VEHICLE}}} can lose money at a red light
emails.subjectAlt: The loss that happens without anything breaking
emails.preheader: Diminished Value Protection is included. Most people have never heard of it. That is the point.
emails.headline:
Somebody taps your
bumper. Your car is
worth less forever.
body: Here is a thing that happens. Someone rear ends you at a light. Their insurance fixes the bumper. The car looks perfect. And it is now worth thousands less, because it has an accident on its history and buyers can read.
That gap is called diminished value. Your plan includes protection for it. Up to $5,000. It is listed on your contract under Also Included, which is a modest place to put something that useful.

hero.label: STILL WAITING ON YOU
hero.fine: The contract already lists Diminished Value Protection. It just does not do anything until the payment clears.

emails.after: No other direct plan we know of includes this. We are not going to name them. You can check. Bring snacks.
emails.cta: Finish it before the red light does →
emails.ps: If you do get rear ended, the other thing to do is take a photo of their plate. We cover the value. We cannot cover forgetting to do that.

emails.goal: Roadside, rental, trip interruption. The breakdown day benefits.
emails.subject: Breakdowns never check your calendar
emails.subjectAlt: The expensive part of breaking down is not the car
emails.preheader: Roadside, a rental, and a hotel if you are far from home. Included.
emails.headline:
The car dying is the
cheap part. The rest of
the day is the bill.
body: A breakdown is not one problem. It is a tow, then a rental, then two days of asking people for rides, then possibly a hotel because it happened three hundred miles from your bed.
The plan handles that part too. It was built by people who have stood on a shoulder at 11pm and would like you to have a better evening than they did.

card.title: ON A BAD DAY
rows: Up to $450 if you are far from home

hero.label: THE WHOLE PLAN, STILL
hero.fine: {{{DOWN}}} down to turn it on. Roadside starts working the moment it is active.

emails.after: None of this requires a good attitude on the day. It requires the plan to be active, which requires the payment, which requires about forty seconds.
emails.ctaNote: Same contract. Same numbers. New level of calm.
emails.ps: The roadside number goes in your phone under R. You will thank a past version of yourself.

emails.goal: Remove the commitment fear. 30 day full refund, prorated after, transferable.
emails.subject: The exit is unlocked. That is why the door is easy.
emails.subjectAlt: Thirty days to decide you were wrong about us
emails.preheader: Full refund in 30 days if no claim has been paid. Prorated after that. No hostage situation.
emails.headline:
We left the exit
unlocked on purpose.
body: Some people stop at the payment step because it feels like signing up for a gym. Five years of something you cannot get out of.
This is not that. Cancel in the first 30 days with no paid claim and you get every dollar back. Cancel after that and it is prorated. Sell the {{{VEHICLE}}} and the coverage can go with it.

card.title: IF YOU CHANGE YOUR MIND
rows: Prorated refund, less a fee where your state allows

hero.label: WHAT IT TAKES TO TRY IT
hero.fine: You can run the whole 30 day test for the price of the first payment. If we were worried about that, we would not offer it.

emails.after: A company that locks the door is telling you something about the room. We would rather you walk in, look around, and decide to stay.
emails.ctaNote: Reopens your checkout. The clock starts when it is active.
emails.ps: Transferable coverage also makes your {{{VEHICLE}}} easier to sell later. Buyers like a car that comes with a plan. We would say that, but it also happens to be true.

emails.goal: Own the no call center promise. The online model is the product.
emails.subject: Nobody from DriveOne Direct is going to call you
emails.subjectAlt: This email is the salesperson. It is not very pushy.
emails.preheader: No hold music, no manager to check with, no Tuesday callback. The whole thing is online.
emails.headline:
This email is the
salesperson. It gets
paid in clicks.
body: You already know what buying coverage usually feels like. Somebody reads a script. Somebody checks with a manager who does not exist. Somebody calls you on a Tuesday while you are in a meeting.
We took all of that out. There is no call center. There is no one assigned to you. There is a payment page, which you have seen, and a link to it, which is below.

card.title: WHO YOU WILL ACTUALLY TALK TO

hero.label: SAME AS DAY ONE
hero.fine: Still the plan you built for your {{{VEHICLE}}}. Still waiting. Still not calling you about it.

emails.after: Open the link at 11pm in a kitchen if that is when you have forty seconds. It does not care what you are wearing.
emails.cta: Finish it without talking to anyone →
emails.ps: We are aware that an email saying nobody will contact you is, itself, contact. We have made peace with it.

video.title: What buying this online actually looks like
video.line: One phone, one checkout, start to finish. Nobody calls. Nobody checks with a manager.

emails.goal: Graceful close. No fake deadline. Leave the door open and stop.
emails.subject: Last one, then we will leave you alone
emails.preheader: This is the last email in the series. The contract stays written. We stop writing.
emails.headline:
We said we would stop.
This is us stopping.
body: Ten emails is enough. Either you are going to finish the payment or you are not, and a seventh reminder about roadside assistance was never going to be the thing that decided it.

So here is where it stands. The contract for your {{{VEHICLE}}} is still written. Checkout still opens from the link below, with your vehicle and term filled in. If pricing for your vehicle changes in the future, the page will tell you before you pay, not after.

hero.label: ONE MORE TIME
hero.sub: then {{{MONTHLY}}} a month at 0% APR for {{{TERM}}}
hero.fine: No deadline. No countdown. Just the last time we put it in front of you.

emails.after: If the answer is no, thank you for reading ten of these. That is more attention than most of our competitors get in a year, and we do not even have a mascot.
emails.ctaNote: Works today. Works next month. We just will not be the ones reminding you.
emails.ps: You are welcome back any time. Nobody will say we told you so. Mostly because nobody here will know.
